post.description:

post.summary: Body: { "refresh_token": "...", "device_name": "...", "device_kind": "..." }
post.description:
Body: { "refresh_token": "...", "device_name": "...", "device_kind": "..." }

A second, independent session for the same account, for a helper that
runs apart from the app that signed in — the Mac's Finder extension
(docs/file-sync-plan.md §7.1). Both then refresh on their own; sharing one
chain would have them present each other's rotated tokens, which reads as
theft and revokes it. The presented token is checked like a refresh but not
rotated. Holding a refresh token already means holding the account, so this
grants nothing new; the new device shows in the session list and can be
signed out on its own.

200.description: Tokens for a new, independent device session

say who may hear one item
(family_admin only).

The other direction from `PUT /members/{id}/grants`, over the same `content_grants` rows: that
one answers "what may this person reach", this one answers "who may reach this". An admin
looking at a book thinks the second way, and had no way to say it.

Owners and family admins are filtered out rather than rejected. `audio2_can_access` gives them
access unconditionally, so a request that leaves one out is not refused — it just cannot take
away what the rule grants, and the response says so by still reporting them as listeners.

post.description:
A member who cannot hear a family-shared item asks the family's admins to change that, rather
than the item just staying invisible with no way to act on it. Notifies every admin — a family
has no single "owner of permissions", and a request only one admin happens to see is not much
better than no request feature.

No de-duplication: a second tap sends a second notification. Acceptable for a household-sized
family and simpler than a request log; the client disables the button once it succeeds so a
double-click is the only realistic repeat, not a real gap.

One request that returns everything a cached client needs to catch up:
changed content of every kind plus tombstones for deletions. Built for
mobile, where re-fetching whole lists over cellular is the thing to avoid.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description:
RFC3339 timestamp from the previous sync's `now`. Omitted ⇒ a full
snapshot, which is what a first run wants.

a dependency that returned 500s for a spell when the upstream started
rejecting requests with no User-Agent.

precisely when the metadata service is down and nobody is watching, which
is the worst possible moment to quietly resume shipping search terms to a
third party. An unreachable catalogue is an error.

flagged.description:
A pattern worth a look: more restored in 30 days than the whole
library holds, or one item restored more than three times. Restores
already pay for their days in the trash (docs/file-sync-plan.md §2
item 12), so this is for noticing, not for blocking.

web_client_id.description: Services ID for Sign in with Apple JS; `None` until configured.

full_name.description:
The user's name, sent by the client only on their first-ever
authorization (Apple's own privacy rule, not ours) — `None` on every
later sign-in.

ApplyIdentifyRequest.description:
Body of `POST /audiobooks/{id}/metadata/apply`. Only the volume id crosses
the wire: the server re-fetches the volume rather than trusting a client's
copy of a search result.

fields.description:
Which parts of the match to actually write. Absent means all of them,
so a client with no field picker still behaves sensibly.

locked.description:
True when access cannot be taken away: the item's owner, or a family admin. A client
should show the state and no control, rather than a control that silently does nothing.

measured.description: Tracks measured at the current extractor version.

total.description: Tracks in this family's library worth measuring.

running.description: True while there is queued work — what a client shows a bar for.

source.description: "Wikimedia Commons", or `None` for a picture set by hand.

unsized_objects.description:
Referenced objects with no recorded size — counted as zero bytes, so a
non-zero value here means `total_bytes` is an undercount.

BookCandidate.description: One search hit, already flattened out of Google's `volumeInfo` nesting.

subtitle.description:
Google keeps this out of `title`; audio2 has no subtitle column, so it
is shown to help tell two editions apart and then dropped.

author.description: Joined with ", " — audio2 stores one author string per book.

cover_url.description:
Best image Google offered, already upgraded past the 128 px thumbnail
where possible. May still 404 — treat a failed load as "no cover".

score.description:
0–100, computed here rather than by Google, which returns relevance
order but no score. See [`score`].

position_secs.description: Counted across the whole book, so a client can divide it by the book's total duration.

file_id.description: Which file the position below is in — what resuming has to seek to.

file_position_secs.description:
The raw stored position inside `file_id`, which is what `PUT .../progress` writes and
what a player seeks to. `position_secs` is the same moment measured from the start of
the book; a client that only syncs the shelf has no file list to convert between them.

updated_at.description:
Whoever wrote last wins. A device holding an unsent position of its own compares against
this before letting the server's value replace it.

google_books_volume_id.description: Set once the book has been matched through the identify flow.

visibility.description: `private` or `family` — which folder this book lives in.

is_owner.description: False for family-shared books owned by someone else.

owner_id.description: Whose it is — for acting on a family member's item (a family shortcut).

source.description: `upload` or `folder`; a folder book's files are read-only (API revision 3).

BookWithPath.description: A created book and where it sits in the own.audio folder.

since.description: Echo of the requested cursor (null on a full sync).

now.description:
Pass this back as `since` next time. Taken *before* the queries run,
so a row written mid-request is re-sent rather than skipped.

full_sync.description: True when no cursor was supplied and this is a complete snapshot.

deleted.description: Items removed since `since`, so the client can purge its cache.

path.description: As asked, or with ` (2)` when the owner already has that path.

used_as.description:
What the server did with it: `cover` (became a cover), `lyrics`
(became a track's lyrics), or nothing.

reporter_name.description: `null` when the reporter has since been deleted — the report stands.

oneOf.description:
A personal-use podcast episode translation (podcast-translation-plan.md P9) — the
original episode's own progress and this one are unrelated (different table, different
length audio), so this exists as its own arm rather than reusing `Episode`'s shape.

kind.description:
`email` (default) or `link`. `claim` invites are created only via
`POST /family/members/provision`, never directly.

max_uses.description:
`link` kind only: how many separate accounts may redeem this code
(1–20, default 1). A fridge QR wants more than one.

label.description: Admin-facing note ("fridge QR"); never shown to the invitee.

current.description: True when this is the device making the request.

image_url.description: Resolved image URL: S3 proxy path when downloaded, else raw RSS URL.

has_local.description: True when the audio file has been downloaded into the object store.

progress_secs.description: Saved playback position in seconds (null = never played).

completed.description: True when the user has listened to the whole episode.

size_bytes.description:
From `media_objects`, `null` when `has_local` is false or the checksum job hasn't
caught up yet (mirror-plan B-2).

has_transcript.description:
True when the feed published a `<podcast:transcript>` for this episode — the gate for
docs/podcast-translation-plan.md's translation feature (no speech-to-text, ever; a
missing transcript means the feature simply isn't offered for this episode).

ErrorBody.description: Every error answer: a status code and this body.

error.description: What went wrong, in English; not meant to be matched on.

my_role.description: The calling user's role in this family.

my_user_id.description:
The calling user's own id — lets clients find "myself" in `members`
without threading a separate profile fetch through just for that
(e.g. a "Leave family" button targeting `DELETE /members/{my_user_id}`).

my_can_upload.description:
The caller's own permissions, so a client need not locate itself in
`members` to decide whether to show an upload affordance.

avatar_url.description:
`/api/v1/family/avatar` when the family has set a photo, else `null`.
family_admin-managed, like the name — see `families::upload_avatar`.

total_seconds.description: Absent when the member keeps their statistics private.

hidden.description: True when this member has not shared their statistics.

visibility.description: `private` or `family` — which folder this feed lives in.

is_owner.description: False for family-shared feeds owned by someone else.

owner_id.description: Whose it is — for acting on a family member's item (a family shortcut).

categories.description:
Podcast Index categories, lowercased, or the feed's own iTunes
categories when the catalogue does not know it. Empty is normal — a
feed subscribed while the metadata service was unreachable has none
until the backfill job reaches it, and clients must render fine
without them.

language_base.description:
`language` folded to its subtag. Clients grouping or filtering by
language must use this, not `language`, which is whatever the
publisher wrote.

auto_store.description:
The server stores each new episode by itself, so the family keeps it
even if the feed later drops it (docs/file-sync-plan.md §5.6).

has_transcripts.description:
At least one episode publishes a transcript, so it can be translated.
Filled in by the list and the single-feed read only; false elsewhere.

sha256.description:
Nullable — the `media_checksum` job fills this in asynchronously after upload
(mirror-plan B-2). A downloading client should verify against it when present and fall
back to a size-only check when it isn't.

object_key.description: Key returned by `/uploads/presign` and already PUT to storage.

relative_path.description:
Path within the uploaded folder — decides play order, exactly as in
the multipart manifest.

FromUploadsRequest.description:
Body of `POST /audiobooks/from-uploads` — the direct-to-storage twin of
the multipart `POST /audiobooks/upload`.

cover_object_key.description: Key returned by `/uploads/presign` for the cover, if one was uploaded.

path.description:
The book's folder in the own.audio folder (`Audiobooks/…`), for a
folder put there; each file's `relative_path` is then its path inside
it and is kept as given. A single loose file: `path` is the file and
its `relative_path` is empty. Without `path` the server gives the book
a default folder and names its files.

desktop_client_id.description:
The OAuth client ID native clients use for the loopback+PKCE flow.
`null` while Google sign-in is unconfigured.

web_client_id.description: The web console's client id, `null` while Google sign-in is off.

id_token.description:
One-shot ID token from a client SDK that already completed the OAuth
dance itself. Mutually exclusive with `code` — provide exactly one.

code.description:
Authorization code from the native loopback+PKCE flow (the Mac app's
path). Requires `code_verifier` and `redirect_uri`.

HoldingsResponse.description:
With `kind` and `id`: the devices holding that item. Without: what the
calling device holds.

HoldingsUpdate.description: `PUT /sync/holdings` body: the device's whole set, or a change to it.

IdentifyFields.description:
Per-field opt-out. `narrator` is not here because Google Books has none to
give (see `metadata::google_books`).

IdentifySearchRequest.description:
Body of `POST /audiobooks/{id}/metadata/search`. The book id scopes
visibility only — the query itself is whatever the client sends, because the
books worth identifying are the ones whose stored title and author are wrong.

code.description: The bearer code the invitee redeems. Deliver it out-of-band.

join_url.description:
`{base_url}/join/{code}` when `server.base_url` is configured, else
`null` — clients fall back to building it from their connected origin.

member_user_id.description:
`kind: "claim"` only — the provisioned account this code activates, so
a client can match a pending `MemberResponse` back to its invite (to
re-show the code / offer "regenerate") without a second lookup.

result.description:
Structured output a job chose to report on completion (e.g. the
cleanup sweep's `{"deleted_families": [...]}`) — most job types leave
this null.

status.description:
`valid` | `expired` | `exhausted`. Unknown codes are a plain 404
instead — see decision D6 on what dead codes may reveal.

oneOf.description: `kind = "claim"` only: who this code signs the claimant in as.

device_name.description: Optional device label shown in the session list ("Anna's iPhone").

device_kind.description: One of `web|ios|android|other`; anything else is coerced to `other`.

grants.description: Item-level overrides on top of the defaults.

display_label.description: Optional in-family label ("Dad"); falls back to display_name in UIs.

pending.description: True for a provisioned account nobody has claimed yet.

avatar_url.description:
`/api/v1/users/{user_id}/avatar` when the member has set one, else
`null`. A relative path, same convention as every other cover URL in
this API (e.g. `audiobooks::book_to_response`'s `cover_url`).

MicrosoftProviderInfo.description:
Shaped like [`GoogleProviderInfo`]: the desktop client id is all a native
client needs, because this side holds the secret and does the exchange.

member_id.description: Optional with a container: the book's, show's or album's owner is found here.

preview.description: True: list what would move, change nothing.

ids.description: Apply only these items; all of them when absent.

file_id.description: For audiobook progress: which file is playing.

device_kind.description:
`web`, `ios`, `android`, … — recorded on any session derived from
this save, so stats can break down by platform.

PodcastCategoryCount.description: One catalogue category and how many feeds sit in it.

active_count.description:
Feeds in this category that published within the last year. This is the
number worth showing a user — `feed_count` is mostly abandoned shows.

language.description:
Language subtag (`en`, not `en-US`). Optional, and unset means no
filter.

Deliberately not defaulted to the household's own languages, which is
what this was first sketched as. The catalogue's search takes one
language, households are not reliably monolingual, and a guessed filter
hides results with no visible explanation — the user sees an empty
search box, not a filter they can turn off. The client knows whether it
has a "search all languages" affordance to offer; the server does not,
so the server does not guess.

categories.description: Added 2026-08-29. Additive on the wire — older clients ignore it.

kind.description:
What the object will be used for — decides the key prefix. One of
`audiobook_file`, `audiobook_cover`, `music_track`, `music_cover`,
`companion_file`.

size_bytes.description:
Client-declared size, checked against the storage limit up front so a
doomed 6 GB upload fails immediately instead of at the last byte. The
real size is read back from storage in `complete`.

content_type.description:
Header the client MUST send with exactly this value: it is part of the
signature, and anything else fails with a signature mismatch.

PrivateItem.description: One private item, in the caller's "Soukromé" folder.

cover_url.description: Same URL the item's own list returns; absent when it has no picture.

album.description: Songs only: the album, so a client can group a long list of songs.

login_email.description:
An email-shaped login identifier the admin picks for a member with no
real mailbox (e.g. `lena@maraz.family`). Stored in `users.email` and
used to sign in; no mail is ever sent to it.

invite.description:
A `claim` invite for the new account — show its QR/link/code so the
member can set their own password.

token_suffix.description: Only the tail is echoed back; the full token is a delivery credential.

device_kind.description:
`web`, `ios`, `android`, … — echoed back so another device can show
"playing on your phone".

device_label.description:
Optional human-readable device name (e.g. "Kornel's Pixel"), free-form
and unvalidated — distinguishes two devices of the same `device_kind`
on one account. Never send a raw model id here; omit instead.

updated_at.description: Echo this back on the next write to detect a concurrent change.

invite_code.description:
A family invite code. Presenting a valid one authorizes registration
even when open self-registration is disabled, and joins the new
account to the inviting family.

allow.description: Items this member may play regardless of their default policy.

deny.description: Items this member may not play regardless of their default policy.

recorded.description: Rows actually stored; duplicates from a retry are silently skipped.

part_id.description: Audiobook file or podcast episode, when known.

seconds_listened.description:
Audio actually consumed, which differs from the wall-clock span when
the listener paused or played at a non-1.0 speed.

client_session_id.description:
Client-generated idempotency key. **Send one.** Android WorkManager
and iOS background tasks both retry on failure, and this is what stops
a retried batch from counting twice.

ended_reason.description:
Why playback stopped: `completed`, `skipped`, `stopped` or `replaced`.

Send the fact, not a judgement — how much an early skip counts against
a track is derived here from `seconds_listened`, so that curve can be
retuned without an app update. Omit it when genuinely unknown; a wrong
value teaches the preference model something false, a missing one only
costs a little signal.

can_listen.description:
Who may hear this item, by user id. Anyone left out is denied.

The whole audience, not a delta: an admin editing this list is looking at all of it, and a
patch shape would make two admins on two screens silently overwrite each other field by
field instead of last-write-wins on something they could both see.

setup_complete.description: `true` once an admin user has been created.

container_kind.description: `book`, `album`, `show`, or null for the member's whole kind.

label.description: What the app shows: the book, album or show title, or null for a kind.

device_code.description: The polling credential. Never shown to anyone; only its hash is stored.

user_code.description: The short code shown on the TV and typed by the approver.

verification_url.description:
Where to approve it — shown under the code, and what the QR encodes. Empty when the
server has no `base_url` configured.

by_day_kind.description: `by_day` split by media kind; days without listening are left out.

streak_days.description: Consecutive days ending today with any listening.

completed_items.description: Lifetime count of finished audiobooks, regardless of the requested range.

preview.description: True: say how many episodes and roughly how many bytes, queue nothing.

latest.description: Only the newest this many episodes not stored yet; all of them when absent.

episodes.description: Episodes queued — or, for a preview, that would be.

estimated_bytes.description: A rough size from the episodes' durations at 128 kbit/s; feeds rarely state sizes.

database.description: The configured database is connected and migrations have run.

title.description: Resolved from the owning table; null if the item was deleted.

restore_charge_micro.description:
What restoring it right now would charge, so a client can say so
before the user taps Restore. Zero when charges are off.

sha256.description: Filled by a background job after upload; verify by size until then.

title.description: For messages only; the tree is built from `path`.

path.description: A book's folder, a track's or episode's file — as the owner put it.

files.description:
A book's files, with their path inside its folder. A track, episode
or companion file has one entry with an empty `relative_path`.

oneOf.description: What an album shortcut matches on (§4.4).

reason.description:
`trashed` (in the trash, may come back), `deleted` (gone for good, or
an episode no longer stored), `hidden` (still exists, no longer
visible to you — unshared, or access withdrawn).

me.description:
The caller, named as the family knows them — the name of their own
`Family/<Me>` folder (§2 item 17).

reset.description:
The cursor was too old: drop what you know and rebuild from the items
that follow (the next pages are a full snapshot).

recommendations_enabled.description:
Deliberately only on `/users/me`, and deliberately absent from
`UpdateUserRequest`: an admin can deactivate an account or change its
role, but cannot decide for someone else that their listening may be
used to suggest things.

discovery_languages.description:
Which languages podcast discovery should answer in. Sent whole, not
added to one at a time: it is a list the user edits, and a PATCH that
appends has no way to express "remove the last one". `[]` means every
language, which is the state everyone starts in.

recommendations_enabled.description:
False until the user turns recommendations on. Carried on every
auth response so a client knows before it renders anything —
fetching `/users/me` separately would mean a frame where the app
does not yet know whether it may look at listening history.

discovery_languages.description:
Base subtags (`en`, `cs`) podcast discovery answers in; empty means
every language. Carried on sign-in so a client can show the setting
without a second call.

avatar_url.description:
`/api/v1/users/{id}/avatar` when set, else `null` — same relative-URL
convention every other cover URL in this API uses.

recommendations_enabled.description:
False until the user switches it on. Clients must compute and show
nothing listening-derived while this is false — not compute it and
hide it. There is no server-side derived state either way, which is
what makes the switch honest rather than cosmetic.

discovery_languages.description:
Base subtags (`en`, `cs`). Empty means discovery answers in every
language — see migration 0063.
